---
applyTo: "i18n/**,d2.config.js,src/**/*.ts,src/**/*.tsx"
---

## Internationalization

- **The repository owns `i18n/en.pot`; Weblate owns every `i18n/<lang>.po` and is their only writer.** `d2-app-scripts i18n extract` writes only the template, and the localized output it generates under `src/locales/` is untracked, so there is nothing to restore after a run and no regeneration commit after a drain. Do not hand-edit a catalogue: the change is either overwritten by Weblate's next write or turns into a conflict — and a pull request that does it is **rejected by CI**, by the `catalogue-ownership` job in [`.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`](../workflows/build-and-test.yml), which fails when any `i18n/*.po` in the pull request carries a commit whose committer is not Weblate. So this is enforced rather than merely stated; the failure names each offending file and how to restore it. **Exactly one repository-side edit of those files is on record as legitimate, and it is the last.** The commit that introduced this rule also rewrote all nine catalogue headers, because each had been created from the template and inherited the generator's metadata — a tool name where the project belongs, and timestamps older than the files carrying them. That was possible only in the handover window: the component was registered but had never written to this repository, no drain had happened, and the sole existing translation was already here. The window is closed, and it does not reopen — after it, a repository-side edit of `i18n/<lang>.po` is a defect however well-intentioned, header hygiene included. Anything of that kind goes through Weblate. *(repo-specific)*
- **Always** give a source string a Weblate **explanation** wherever it exposes a translator to markup, a placeholder or an identifier that must survive translation unchanged — an interpolated `{name}`, a format token, an embedded tag — saying which part is fixed and which is theirs to translate. Explanations live only in Weblate's database, so they cost the catalogue nothing and survive every `msgmerge`. **Remove the exposure where the code allows it, and explain it where removing it would cost more than it saves**: a value the user never sees translated belongs outside the string, but a placeholder that has to sit mid-sentence for the grammar to work cannot be moved, so it earns an explanation instead. A quality check rejects the mistake after the fact; the explanation is what prevents it. *(repo-specific)*
- **Always** regenerate `i18n/en.pot` with `yarn build`, **never** with `yarn i18n:extract` alone. The template carries the manifest's strings — the app title, its description and every command-palette shortcut, as `__MANIFEST_*` entries — and `@dhis2/cli-app-scripts` adds them only when the extraction is told it is extracting an app (`cli/src/lib/i18n/extract.js`, the `isApp` branch). Its `build` and `start` commands tell it so; its `i18n extract` command does not. A bare `i18n extract` therefore writes a template **without** them, dropping every translation of the title and the shortcuts on the next Weblate sync, and the diff reads like an ordinary refresh. *(repo-specific)*
